executiveSummary: Election-related synthetic media threats intensified, with U.S. federal authorities issuing back-to-back public advisories warning of convincing deepfake audio/video and AI-enabled phishing targeting campaigns and election officials View Advisory and active fraud schemes impersonating campaigns and officials to solicit donations and personal data View Advisory . A separate report indicates a pending U.S. FCC action could loosen political robocall restrictions, potentially normalizing AI voices in last-minute electoral communications Source . Spain also saw a high-profile deepfake-style political video from a major opposition party ahead of national voting View Article . Criminal misuse continued to drive large financial and public-safety impacts: reports describe a deepfake video-call executive impersonation leading to roughly $25M in enterprise losses in Hong Kong View Article , an estimated €95M voice-clone fraud affecting a major bank in Italy View Article , and cloned-voice vishing that impersonated a Florida sheriff to extort residents View Article . On the national-security front, OpenAI reported disrupting covert "false-front" influence operations that used AI personas and fabricated materials to infiltrate media and online platforms Source . Meanwhile, law-enforcement action in France reportedly targeted deepfake CSAM and non-consensual image sites, indicating ongoing large-scale synthetic exploitation networks. Defensive and provenance developments advanced, including new documentation for verifying C2PA-signed image credentials Source , Android device-level AI defenses against scam calls and messages View Article , and newsroom authenticity workflows combining C2PA and robust watermark recovery View Article . The U.S. judiciary was also warned about deepfake evidence risks, highlighting rising legal-system exposure View Article .
